title: Client script instrumentation and benchmark roadmap
topics: kv cache warmup and cold start
benchmark harness adaptation to customer scripts
summary: Kickoff scoping to adapt StellarRetail customer scripts into Redwood's benchmark harness. Focused on telemetry instrumentation (latency buckets, token-level timing), deciding streaming vs non-streaming paths for their conversational and batch scoring workloads, and defining acceptance gates (p99 latency, throughput, token cost). Agreed on initial pilot: 2-week harness integration, synthetic replay + 24h live-ish soak, and an acceptance checklist including kv-cache warmup procedure and compare-run vs current in-house model infra.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Priya (StellarRetail): Hi, Priya here, Lead ML Eng. Markus, Daniela, Tom also on.
[00:18] Markus: Markus on infra.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Luis is our SE, he'll lead the harness mapping. Luis?
[00:27] Luis (Redwood SE): Hey all, yep. Quick agenda: we want to map your existing client scripts, understand tokenization and streaming usage, add instrumentation hooks so we can measure cold vs warm kv cache behavior, and then agree success criteria and timeline.
[00:45] Daniela: Sounds good, our big pain is unpredictable tail latency and cost spikes during peak search events.
[00:52] Tom: Also want to see realistic replay — not just synthetic short prompts — our sessions are multi-turn, sometimes 20–30 tokens per turn, average session 8 turns.
[01:05] Priya: Important — we have two modes: conversational chat for support (low latency target ~150ms p50, p95 under 450ms for short prompts) and nightly batch rerank job (throughput hundreds of reqs/sec, latency less critical).
[01:25] Speaker 1: is there a note about encryption?
[01:28] Maya: yes, we'll include the security checklist later.
[01:31] Luis: Quick clarifying question on streaming: do you stream partial tokens from client or do you only request streaming on short-turn chat?
[01:40] Priya: For support chat we use streaming so UI shows tokens in real-time. For our reranking it's non-streaming batch.
[01:48] Luis: Got it. For the harness we'll need two flows: streaming path with client-side timeouts and non-streaming bulk load. Implementation differences matter for KV cache warmup and batching.
[02:00] Markus: can you elaborate on the kv-cache warmup? we've seen cold-start p99s spike a lot.
[02:07] Luis: Sure. K V cache — sometimes transcribed as K V — refers to the attention key/value cache that speeds up decoding on long sequences. If a model instance hasn't seen the session prefix, you get a cold warmup penalty: first few tokens are slower and block streaming. We want to instrument token-level timing to measure that.
[02:30] Priya: Nice, so we need metrics like token latency distribution, number of cache misses, and maybe a per-session warmup curve.
[02:38] Luis: Exactly. We'll add counters and histograms: token_latency_ms, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, prefix_bytes. Also we recommend tracing request stages: client->frontdoor, frontdoor->compute, decode time, and network egress.
[02:55] Maya: we'll share a sample instrumentation protobuf and the harness adapter spec after the call — link will be in the follow-up.
[03:03] Daniela: On acceptance criteria — what do you typically put in the POC doc?
[03:09] Luis: For this one, propose: 1) Functional parity with your current infra for responses; 2) Backend p99 latency for conversational under 900ms on accepted traffic slices; 3) Throughput target for rerank within 10% of your baseline cost per 1000 queries; 4) No untriaged errors above 0.1% during a 24h soak.
[03:30] Priya: That p99 target seems loose — our UX team wants p95 < 450ms. Is that possible with streaming?
[03:36] Luis: Streaming changes perceived latency — frontend will see tokens earlier even if backend still finishing. We can meet p95 450ms for most short prompts with the streaming path if kv-cache warmup strategy is applied. We need to validate on their actual distribution.
[03:52] Markus: timeline? how long to get harness running with our scripts?
[03:56] Maya: We suggested two weeks for integration, plus one week for initial runs and analysis. So three weeks to first report.
[04:04] Tom: do you need access to our prod traffic? we can't hand that over.
[04:08] Luis: We don't need prod. We'll run a synthetic replay using a scrubbed sample dataset. Ideally you provide a 1% sample or sanitized logs.
[04:18] Priya: We can provide stored session logs with PII removed. What format?
[04:22] Luis: JSONL with metadata fields: session_id, timestamp, turn_index, prompt_text, response_length_hint, streaming_flag. We'll send the adapter schema.
[04:32] Speaker 1: how do you handle model variants?
[04:34] Luis: We'll run one canonical model to start; can add quantized variants later. For now keep model fixed to baseline you use so comparisons are apples-to-apples.
[04:44] Maya: benchmarks — we plan two passes: a synthetic replay that mirrors token mix and conversation depth, and a 24h soak at reduced scale to validate reliability. We'll also run back-to-back comparison with your in-house infra for cost per 1k tokens.
[04:59] Daniela: On instrumentation, we also want per-request user_id bucketing and goal-based success labels for later quality evals.
[05:07] Luis: Good call — include an optional label field in the JSONL for quality buckets.
[05:12] Priya: Any special config for streaming harness? we saw earlier runs that artificially concatenate prompts and that skews cache behavior.
[05:20] Luis: We'll mirror the session boundaries exactly. For warmup we'll include a controlled warmup window: replay prefixes 1–3 messages before measuring, and run both cold-start traces and warmed instances.
[05:32] Markus: instrumentation overhead? we worry that extra tracing will change numbers.
[05:36] Luis: we use low-overhead histograms and sample traces at 1% — that should be acceptable. We'll note sampling in reports.
[05:46] Maya: logistics: we'll need a shared folder. I'll drop the harness adapter spec and a benchmark template spreadsheet (link below).
[05:55] Maya: link: https://redwood.example/poc/harness-adapter-v2 (intentional placeholder)
[06:01] Daniela: about success criteria — can we add a UX gating item: streaming must deliver first token visible within 200ms for >70% of short prompts?
[06:10] Luis: can do, we'll add a UX-first metric: time_to_first_token_ms p70 < 200. We'll validate with the client-side rendering delays accounted for.
[06:22] Priya: Cost comparison — how is unit cost shown in your report?
[06:26] Maya: We'll show tokenized counts, raw token throughput, estimated dollar-per-1k tokens using both your cloud pricing and Redwood's hosted pricing, and GPU-second breakdown.
[06:36] Tom: any sensitive data handling steps for the logs we share?
[06:39] Maya: yes, signed NDA + secure upload to a customer-specific s3 bucket with KMS. We'll follow SOC2 controls.
[06:47] Speaker 1: competitors? we had a run with AuroraAI and their tails were worse.
[06:51] Luis: noted. We'll include a competitors_mentioned section in the notes.
[06:55] Maya: ok let's talk deliverables and owners.
[07:00] Luis: I'll own the harness adapter changes and initial run scripts. Maya will own commercial/discussion and security path. Priya will provide sanitized logs and the target metric thresholds. Markus will validate networking inspection and sampling.
[07:15] Daniela: timeline recap?
[07:17] Maya: Week 0 (this week): share adapter spec and template. Week 1–2: customer engineers adapt scripts and provide sample logs; Redwood implements adapter and runs test harness. Week 3: analysis and comparison report; Week 4 optional soak and acceptance.
[07:36] Priya: sounds good. can we schedule a mid-integration check?
[07:39] Maya: yes, 30-minute sync at end of Week 1. I'll propose times.
[07:45] Tom: any reason to run a canary in our VPC?
[07:48] Luis: we can discuss a private deployment canary later but for POC we avoid VPC complexity; synthetic replay on Redwood hosted or dedicated pool is faster.
[07:59] Speaker 1: small question: do you do model caching per-tenant?
[08:03] Luis: caching is per-instance not per-tenant; we can pin instances for tenancy in Dedicated mode if needed.
[08:14] Maya: ok wrapping up, I'll send minutes and links. Thanks all.
[08:19] Priya: thanks, bye.
[08:21] End of recording.
